panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Panel A shows full-body views of proband with FERMT1 variation causing Kindler syndrome; caption describes xerosis, erythematous patches and hyperpigmentation consistent with poikiloderma. B: Posterior neck close-up of same FERMT1 proband showing erythema and hyperpigmentation described for Kindler syndrome. C: Anterior neck/chest of same proband showing erythematous patches and hyperpigmentation attributed to Kindler syndrome. D: Oral close-up of FERMT1 Kindler proband with captioned malocclusion, dental dysmorphology, swollen gums and angular cheilitis; gingival and oral mucosal involvement maps to vocabulary. E: Dorsal hands of same proband showing captioned cigarette paper-like atrophic wrinkling classic for Kindler syndrome. F: Dorsal feet of same proband showing captioned atrophy with cigarette-paper wrinkles, dystrophic nails and thickened stratum corneum/keratoderma of Kindler syndrome.

in_text_mentions: valuation of the newborn revealed extensive areas of denudation, skin fragility and erosions. Blister formation on the frontal region of the face was observed, as well as denudation areas and periorificial involvement. The lower and upper limbs presented significant areas of denudation, multiple superficial erosions, and haemorrhagic blisters, as well as skin fragility. The clinical presentation of the lower limbs suggested Bart syndrome. The skin surrounding the lesions was erythematous and fragile. Nail dystrophy and nail absence were observed. No other anomalies were recorded (Figure 1a–f).

in_text_mentions: Physical examination revealed generalized poikiloderma with widespread hypo- and hyperpigmented patches over the face, neck, axillae, and extremities (Figure 2). The skin was thin, wrinkled, and atrophic, particularly on the hands and feet, resulting in loss of fingerprints and impaired finger movement. Additional findings included nail dystrophy, erythematous scaly plaques on flexor surfaces, digital banding, and localized hyperkeratosis (Figure 3).

pigmentary incontinence with melanin deposition in the dermis

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: H&E biopsy from 24-year-old Kindler Syndrome case; caption states epidermal atrophy and subepidermal cleft formation, supporting atrophy correlate of Kindler Syndrome. b: Same KS leg biopsy; caption states focal vacuolar degeneration of basal layer and epidermal thinning, supporting atrophic component. c: Same KS leg biopsy; caption states pigmentary incontinence with melanin deposition, pigmentary component of poikiloderma. d: Same KS leg biopsy; caption states dilated superficial dermal blood vessels, vascular/telangiectatic component of poikiloderma histology.
panels.attribution_text: Ahmad et al. Kindler Syndrome in a 24-Year-Old Male: A Clinical Diagnosis in the Absence of Genetic Testing: A Rare Case Report.. Case reports in dermatological medicine 2025. doi:10.1155/crdm/9343494. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological features of the skin biopsy (hematoxylin and eosin stain). (a) Low-power view (40x) showing epidermal atrophy and subepidermal cleft formation. (b) Low-power view (100x) highlighting focal vacuolar degeneration of the basal layer and overlying epidermal thinning. (c) High-power view (200x) revealing pigmentary incontinence with melanin deposition in the dermis. (d) High-power view (400x) demonstrating dilated superficial dermal blood vessels.
in_text_mentions: Histological findings: An incisional biopsy from the leg showed epidermal atrophy, dilated superficial dermal vessels, focal vacuolar degeneration at the basal layer, subepidermal cleft formation, and pigmentary incontinence (Figure 5). The biopsy was taken when the patient was 24 years old, thus representing a late stage of the disease. Accordingly, the histological picture reflected chronic changes. While these findings are supportive, they are not pathognomonic for KS and can be seen in other hereditary bullous poikiloderma syndromes.
